newsitem.title: USA: US Rep Archer concerned on inflation-indexed bonds.
newsitem.headline: US Rep Archer concerned on inflation-indexed bonds.

text.p: House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer, R-Texas, said Monday he was concerned about inflation-indexed bonds that the Treasury Department planned to issue later this month.
"I've got a great concern about that because it leaves open how much our debt service charges are going to be in the future; it does not give us any certainty at all," Archer said at a briefing.
The Treasury planned to hold its first auction of inflation-indexed debt on Jan. 29. The bonds are tied to movements in the consumer price index.
"Now when we issue bonds we can project accurately what our debt-service charges are going to be," Archer said.

"If we go to these inflation-indexed bonds, we will never know what the debt service charge is going to be from one year to the next, because we can never know for sure what inflation is going to be," he added.

The Social Security advisory council in its report said it supported the Treasury's plan to offer inflation-indexed bonds. "The council believes these bonds would make it easier to plan for retirement by translating lump sum accumulations into inflation-protected retirement income flows."
